name: Biogas upgrading to biomethane
principle: CO2 is removed from biogas to reach pipeline-grade biomethane using water scrubbing, PSA, membranes, amine scrubbing or cryogenic separation. IEA Bioenergy Task 37 lists methane slip as below 0.1% for amines, 0.5 to 1% for membranes, 1 to 2% for water scrubbing and PSA, and 2 to 4% for physical adsorption.

performance.basis: amine 0.04 to 0.1% (lowest); membrane 0.5 to 1%; water scrubber 1 to 2%; PSA below 2%; physical adsorption 2 to 4%; cryogenic about 2%

source.note: IEA Bioenergy Task 37, Methane slip from biogas upgrading (January 2023)

performance.metric: biogas upgrading energy use by technology
performance.unit: kWh per Nm3 raw biogas (water scrubbing about 0.4-0.5, reducible to about 0.3 in advanced designs; PSA 0.15-0.3; membranes 0.2-0.4; amine wash regeneration adds 0.1-0.15 kWh/Nm3)
performance.basis: PG&E technical analysis (2 Jul 2018): water/chemical scrubbing needs about 0.4-0.5 kWh/Nm3 raw biogas; Bauer et al. SGC report: PSA electricity 0.15-0.3 kWh/Nm3; Wantz et al. 2023: high-pressure water scrubber measured 0.8 kWh/Nm3, reducible to 0.3; Khan et al. 2021 review (OSTI): amine regeneration adds 0.1-0.15 kWh/Nm3

source.note: PG&E Water/Chemical Scrubbing Technical Analysis, 2 Jul 2018; Bauer SGC 2013; Wantz 2023; Khan 2021; read 2026-10-28

advantages: Amine upgrading has the lowest methane slip
limitations: Slip control for small plants is costly

sources.note: IEA Bioenergy Task 37, Methane slip from biogas upgrading (January 2023)
